Raid **lockouts** in **World of Warcraft (WoW)** are a mechanism that prevents players from repeating the same **raid** instance multiple times within a certain period, typically a week, to encourage players to participate in other activities and balance the game’s content. The **lockout** system is based on the **raid ID**, which is assigned to a player or a group when they enter a **raid** instance, and it determines the **lockout** period and the **loot** eligibility for each player.

## Understanding Raid Lockouts

To understand how **raid lockouts** work, it’s essential to know the different types of **raid** instances and their corresponding **lockout** rules.
In **WoW**, **raids** can be categorized into several types, including **Normal**, **Heroic**, **Mythic**, and **Raid Finder**, each with its own **lockout** mechanism.

### Types of Lockouts

There are two primary types of **lockouts**: **loot-based lockouts** and **ID-based lockouts**. **Loot-based lockouts** allow players to repeat a **raid** instance multiple times, but they can only receive **loot** once per **lockout** reset. On the other hand, **ID-based lockouts** bind a player to a specific **raid ID**, preventing them from entering the same **raid** instance with a different group until the **lockout** reset.

## Frequently Asked Questions

The following are some frequently asked questions about **raid lockouts** in **WoW**:

1. **Can I do a normal and heroic raid in the same week?**: Yes, you can defeat each **raid** boss once per week per character, but you’ll need to do so on two different characters if you want to do both a 10- and 25-person **raid** in a single week.

...

**How do raid lockouts work in Wotlk Classic?**: In **WotLK Classic**, once tied to an instance **ID**, you may not enter any other versions of that **raid** of that difficulty until your **raid lock** resets.
14. **What is the best WoW raid of all time?**: According to many players, the best **WoW** **raid** of all time is **Ulduar**, which offers a unique and challenging experience with its corrupted **Titan Keepers** and **Yogg-Saron**.
15. **Can you do a normal and heroic raid in the same week on the same character?**: No, you cannot do a **normal** and **heroic** **raid** in the same week on the same character, as you can only receive **loot** once per **lockout** reset per character.

By understanding how **raid lockouts** work in **WoW**, players can better plan their **raid** strategies and maximize their **loot** potential. Whether you’re a seasoned **raider** or a new player, knowing the **lockout** rules and mechanisms can enhance your overall **WoW** experience.

* If you enter an instance that is more progressed than your own and get saved to it, you will be locked to all prior bosses.

### Strict Instance-based Lockout [ [](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwowpedia.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FRaid_lockout%3Faction%3Dedit%26section%3D4&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit") ]

_Used for: All classic raids ( Molten Core through Sunwell ), Heroic difficulty of Wrath of the Lich King raids through Throne of Thunder, and all Mythic difficulty raids._

* Progress is tied to a fixed instance ID. Once tied to an instance ID, you may not enter any other versions of that raid of that difficulty until your raid lock resets.
* If other players complete that instance while you are absent, the instance will be empty for you as well, because progress is tied to the instance, and not your character.
* You may not switch between 10-player and 25-player raid size once locked to one size or the other (does not apply to Mythic which is 20-player only).

> what has changed?

Vanilla raid lockouts were treated like mythic raid lockouts are on live.  
  
Meaning once you kill a boss or enter a raid instance where any boss is dead, you are saved to that Raid ID. Any attempt to enter that raid instance prior to the scheduled raid reset causes you to enter that particular Raid ID.  
  
This means that if you pug and only kill one boss, you cannot then join your guild run the next day to kill the rest of the bosses.  
  
It also means that if you're doing a progression run and only kill 1 boss, a pug you brought in could steal the raid ID and go kill the rest of the bosses before your next guild raid night.
